newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's foreign reserves rise to $15.379 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's foreign reserves rise to $15.379 bln.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves rose $200 million, or 1.3 percent, to $15.379 billion in the week to January 7, according to figures released by the Central Bank.
Reserves were up from $15.179 on December 30, the bank's weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
Boosted by large capital inflows stemming from high international oil prices, Venezuela's foreign reserves rose over $5 billion last year.
This comfortably overshot the government's original target of a growth by only $1.5 billion in 1996, as part of Venezuela's IMF-supported economic adjustment program launched mid-April.
In 1995, Venezuela's reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, to end the year at $9.723 billion.
